clue.text: What one must pay for purchases from cat shops?

definitions.text: What one must pay for purchases

indicators.note: the letters are made from the words cat shops, rearranged into a new phrase

explanation.surface: A question about how a customer settles the bill at a pet shop that sells cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that the answer is made out of the letters of CAT SHOPS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money handed over at the moment of sale is payment due on any purchase made without credit.

clue.text: Put down for an indoor game?

explanation.surface: A question whether a dismissive phrase also names something played indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush or suppress someone is to put them down, and the racket sport played in a walled court is an indoor game.

clue.text: A flower held in high esteem or reprimanded

definitions.text: A flower held in high esteem

parts.note: taken as written
chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or reprimand

explanation.surface: A blossom that is either prized or told off.
explanation.definitionFit: The exotic bloom is famously prized by growers and collectors, a flower of high status.

clue.text: A footnote on Red Indian fellows who are thoroughly disliked!

indicators.note: in a down clue the footnote piece is placed on, that is below, the first piece

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people (the clue uses the dated term)
PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A remark added under a description of tribesmen who are widely loathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Indian' is a dated term the setter uses for a Native American people; in a down clue 'on' means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant, obnoxious men are called creeps, people widely detested.

clue.text: Not against change that will prevent the economy from moving

definitions.text: that will prevent the economy from moving
definitions.note: a clause describing a state; the answer is the noun for that state

indicators.note: to change the words Not against is to rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: An economist's warning that a policy shift, far from helping, will bring the economy to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns the letters of NOT AGAINST into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic standstill, with no growth or activity, is the condition that keeps an economy from moving.

clue.text: Designing fellow who eats out

parts.note: a scheming man who dines at restaurants, read instead as an engraver whose acid eats lines out of a metal plate to make a design

explanation.surface: A scheming man who likes dining in restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designing' suggests scheming and 'eats out' dining, but the artist makes designs and the acid he uses eats into the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A printmaker biting a design into a plate with acid is a craftsman whose acid eats out the lines.

clue.text: Across section of the church

parts.note: read as a cross section, a slice through a building, but meaning the part of a church that runs across it

explanation.surface: An architect's cross-sectional drawing of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Across' as 'A cross': the arms of a cruciform church run across the nave.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cross-shaped church the arm lying at right angles to the nave is the section that runs across.

clue.text: A kind of jazz one may expect to hear when the band has warmed up

definitions.text: A kind of jazz one may expect to hear when the band has warmed up

parts.words: A kind of jazz one may expect to hear when the band has warmed up
parts.note: a warmed-up band would literally produce heated playing, which is the name of an energetic early jazz style

explanation.surface: A jazz fan waits for the band to get into its stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmed up' is taken literally: a band that is warm plays warm, or heated, sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic, improvised 1920s jazz was given a name meaning heated playing.

clue.text: A magazine in colour given a new lease of life?

definitions.text: given a new lease of life

indicators.note: the magazine piece goes in the colour piece

parts.note: red is a colour
a magazine is a store, as for arms or ammunition

explanation.surface: A periodical reprinted in colour is revived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a periodical but here means a storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brought back to its former good condition has been given a new lease of life.

clue.text: Devious man's clue for an avuncular New World figure

indicators.note: a devious route twists about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crafty fellow's hint pointing towards a kindly American personification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' rearranges the letters of MANS CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded personification of the United States government is an uncle, hence avuncular, and American.

clue.text: Devout-looking insect not in favour of cutting a scrip?

indicators.note: the opposing piece cuts into the written-document piece, sitting between its letters

parts.note: a scrip is a small written paper; MS stands for manuscript, a written document
to be anti something is to oppose it

explanation.surface: An insect that seems pious but objects to cutting a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' places ANTI between M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying insect holds its forelegs as if in prayer, so it looks devout.

clue.text: Absenting oneself from light training?

explanation.surface: A question whether missing sessions counts as easy exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing a class is cutting it, and jumping a rope is light exercise boxers use in training.

clue.text: Bogus fees held back by the Post Office

indicators.note: the reversed fees are held inside the abbreviation for the Post Office

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office

indicators.note: the word dues is turned to read backwards

parts.note: dues are fees, such as membership charges

explanation.surface: Counterfeit charges kept back by postal officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' and 'back' work separately: one turns the fees round, the other wraps the postal abbreviation around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham or false thing is fake, pretended rather than genuine.

clue.text: Abnormally neat and decent sort of prior

indicators.note: abnormally means in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A remarkably tidy and respectable kind of monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abnormally' rearranges NEAT and DECENT. 'prior' looks like a monk but here means earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going before in time is earlier, as a precedent is.

clue.text: Whatever the cost, it could make a nice party (2.3.5) 181 across going to the first three backers?

indicators.note: the words a nice party could make something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A host ready to spend any sum for a good gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges A NICE PARTY. The clue as held runs on into the next clue's text.
explanation.definitionFit: However much it costs, regardless of expense: an idiom for paying anything.

clue.text: The order of jesting bedmakers?

parts.note: the phrase for perfect neatness shares its name with the prank of folding a sheet so the bed cannot be got into

explanation.surface: A question about how a company of joking chambermaids arranges things.
explanation.walkthrough: The prank bed with a folded-back sheet is named after a dessert, as is the phrase for perfect tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat, tidy arrangement is described with this phrase, which also names the practical-joke bed.

clue.text: Alarming trouble on the border

indicators.note: to trouble a word is to disturb its letters

explanation.surface: Worrying unrest at a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ALARMING.
explanation.definitionFit: At the edge or borderline, as a seat won by a slim majority is described.

clue.text: They don't believe he requires foreign capital

indicators.note: the first piece requires the second to follow it

parts.note: taken as written
Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: Doubters say a man needs money from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign capital' suggests overseas money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagans and unbelievers hold no faith in the god of the main religions.

clue.text: I across going to the first three backers?

definitions.text: I across going to the first three backers?

parts.words: I across going to the first three backers?
parts.note: 1 across is a cross-reference to ready money, and here that cash goes to those who backed the horses finishing in the top three

explanation.surface: A betting-shop question about who collects the winnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is a misreading of 1: 1 across is ready money. The backers are punters, and a horse in the first three is placed.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnings paid on a horse that finishes in the top three, as each-way and place bets pay out.

clue.text: Gunners brought in with spirit .

indicators.note: the gunners are brought in to the word with, sitting among its letters

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, RA, are known as the Gunners

explanation.surface: Artillerymen arriving full of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery are traditionally called the Gunners; 'with' looks like a link word but supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or apparition, especially one seen just before death, is a spirit.

clue.text: … in case the Engineers C fold

indicators.note: the Engineers piece goes in the word case

parts.note: taken as written
RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A warning in case the military engineers give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like giving up, as a business folds, but is a line pressed into cloth or paper. The stray C in the clue as held is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A line or ridge made by folding is a fold in fabric or paper.

clue.text: Add a couple of pages, then stop

parts.note: pp is the abbreviation for pages
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: Advice to write a little more and then finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach something at the end of a document is to add it.

clue.text: Clues for cats and dogs to get their teeth into, perhaps

definitions.text: for cats and dogs to get their teeth into, perhaps

explanation.surface: Puzzle clues pictured as something for pets to chew on.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword entries are called by this name, and animal lungs, sold as pet food, share it.

clue.text: A sweet pea Rex let fall

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Rex, king
to drop is to let fall

explanation.surface: The king drops a sweet pea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet pea' reads as a flower, but 'A sweet' is the definition. R is Rex, Latin for king, used on British coins and documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped boiled confection with a fruity flavour is a sweet.

clue.text: Type of fruit basket to make word-play clear?

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: A fruit container that turns out to be a source of puns.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNNET is the British word for a small basket of soft fruit such as strawberries.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square container of thin wood or plastic holds soft fruit like berries.

clue.text: Exhibit doubt when the tea is freshly brewed

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a fresh pot of tea is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly brewed' rearranges THE TEA IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause in uncertainty before acting is to show doubt.

clue.text: Decide to become militant, maybe

parts.note: taking up militancy suggests protest, but the real sense is choosing to become a soldier

explanation.surface: An activist resolves to turn radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'militant' suggests a protester; here it means military, joining up.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for the armed forces is choosing to become a soldier.

clue.text: He comes in to wait in the finish

indicators.note: the He piece comes in to the waiting piece, among its letters

parts.note: to attend means to wait on or serve
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man arrives to wait until things are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wait' here means to serve, as a waiter attends on diners; 'the finish' with 'in' gives the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally, when all is done, is the sense of this idiom.
